stories.headline: Blinken openly highlighted China’s triple manufacturing output, massive domestic consumer base, and expanding edge in technological innovation and patents,
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Blinken acknowledged China's significant advancements in manufacturing, domestic consumption, and technological innovation. China's manufacturing output has tripled, and its domestic consumer base is massive. The country is also expanding its edge in technological innovation and patents. Meanwhile, China is on track to execute its "Triple Output" AI Strategy, aiming to triple its domestic production of artificial intelligence processors by 2026. Despite this, China still lags behind in strategic technologies like computer chips and aircraft. The country has defended its manufacturing sector, rejecting criticism of excessive capacity, and citing its benefits to the world. China has maintained its position as the world's largest manufacturer for 15 consecutive years, demonstrating remarkable growth and resilience in its manufacturing sector. The US has imposed higher tariffs on China, amid ongoing trade tensions.

stories.headline: "The Iran and Ukraine wars may be connecting."
stories.summary: Iran and Ukraine's conflicts may be connecting, with recent incidents sparking concerns. Ukraine targeted an Iranian cargo vessel in the Caspian Sea, prompting Iran to threaten retaliation. This incident followed Israel's targeting of Iran's Caspian naval presence in March. Russia and Iran have vowed to retaliate against the latest strikes, escalating tensions. The Caspian Sea is becoming a volatile intersection of the two conflicts, threatening international trade and stability. Experts warn that Ukraine's actions may be an attempt to expand the conflict and draw in the US and Europe. The situation is complex, with the US involved in a joint war with Israel against Iran, while also being impacted by Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The overlap of these conflicts has raised concerns among policymakers, with some warning of further chaos and instability in the region.

stories.headline: At least 38 Nigerien soldiers were reportedly killed in two separate attacks by suspected Islamic State fighters on military positions in Niger, raising
stories.summary: At least 38 Nigerien soldiers were killed in two separate attacks by suspected Islamic State fighters on military positions in Niger. The attacks occurred on July 31, with 17 members of the Nigerien Defence and Security Forces killed in one incident and 21 in another. Islamic State fighters are suspected to be responsible for the attacks. Niger faces threats from both Islamic State and Boko Haram insurgents, with the latter active in the country's southeastern regions. The country has experienced several deadly attacks in recent years, including a 2019 incident in which over 70 soldiers were killed. The latest attacks highlight the ongoing security challenges in Niger and the region. The incidents are part of a broader insurgency that has affected several countries, including Nigeria, where Boko Haram originated in 2009.

stories.headline: Police are investigating a suspicious fire that broke out overnight at a kosher restaurant in Montreal's Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough.
stories.summary: A suspicious fire broke out overnight at Nöam, a kosher restaurant in Montreal's Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough. The fire, which caused extensive damage, is being investigated as a possible arson by Montreal police. Firefighters responded to the blaze on Décarie Blvd. around 3:15 a.m. A possible suspect was seen walking away from the scene. The incident has raised concerns in the community that it may have been motivated by hate. The restaurant, known for its Italian and Mediterranean cuisine, was devastated by the fire. Police are investigating the incident and reviewing evidence to determine the cause of the fire and potential motives. The investigation is ongoing, with no official determination yet on whether the fire was a hate crime or not.

stories.headline: TORRAS Unveils Q3 Air Pro, the World's First Dual-Layer Airbag Case Built for Outdoor Adventure
stories.summary: TORRAS has unveiled the Q3 Air Pro, the world's first dual-layer airbag case designed for outdoor adventure. Building on four generations of airbag innovation, the Q3 Air Pro features a newly engineered dual-layer airbag system for enhanced protection. This flagship case is more than a phone accessory, it's protective gear designed to help adventurers perform at their best in demanding environments. The Q3 Air Pro utilizes TORRAS's proprietary X-SHOCK airbag technology, which combines a slim form with superior shock absorption. This technology allows for a slim and lightweight design while maintaining exceptional protection for the device. The Q3 Air Pro is the latest development in TORRAS's airbag innovation, providing a unique solution for outdoor enthusiasts who need reliable protection for their devices in extreme conditions. The case is designed to provide superior protection and peace of mind for adventurers.

stories.headline: There's a 40-year-old bug in every copy of Excel and Microsoft says it will never fix it
stories.summary: A 40-year-old bug in Microsoft Excel incorrectly identifies 1900 as a leap year. The issue originated from Lotus 1-2-3, a predecessor to Excel, and was deliberately retained by Microsoft for backwards compatibility. To replicate the bug, users can type "60" into a cell, format it as a date, and Excel will display February 29, 1900. Although the bug's practical impact is limited to dates before March 1, 1900, it can still cause data-integrity issues in historical analyses and automated pipelines. Microsoft has chosen not to fix the bug, citing the potential disruption it would cause to existing spreadsheets and applications. As a result, the bug remains present in all versions of Excel, including Excel 365, and has become a lasting legacy of the software's early development. The bug has been acknowledged by Microsoft, but no plans to correct it have been announced.

stories.headline: Now you can invest in Crimson Desert - update 1.16.00 released with new goods and trading posts
stories.summary: Pearl Abyss has released update 1.16.00 for Crimson Desert, introducing significant changes to the game's trading system. The update adds 133 new trading posts, increasing opportunities for players to buy and sell goods. The average buy price for trade goods is now displayed, and players can register items to the map item filter for easier tracking. The update also improves the map, showing trade goods' quantities on horses and wagons. Additionally, the game's wagon trading system has been reworked, offering dynamic prices and a new investment layer through the bank. This update aims to make trading a more lucrative activity, with quadrupled profits available. The patch notes also mention the addition of FSR 4.1, enhancing the game's overall experience. These changes are available in the latest version of the game, listed as 1.000.423 on consoles.

stories.headline: Virtual Boy (Cardboard Model) sees discount in Australia and Japan
stories.summary: The Virtual Boy (Cardboard Model) has received a price reduction in Australia and Japan. In Australia, the discount lowers the price from $29.95 AUD to $19.95 AUD, available until August 17, 2026, with shipping fees applying. This offer follows the model's initial release in Australia on February 17, 2026, as a more affordable alternative to the standard Virtual Boy. A similar sale is also being offered in Japan, although the exact discounted price is not specified. The cardboard model was initially made available for pre-order on the Nintendo Store in Australia, alongside the standard Virtual Boy, starting September 13, 2025. This is the first time Nintendo has offered a discount on the cardboard model Virtual Boy.

stories.headline: Giants suspend Harrison Bader's pay after late-night scooter crash
stories.summary: The San Francisco Giants have suspended Harrison Bader's pay following a late-night scooter crash that worsened his existing foot injury. Bader, who signed a two-year, $20.5 million contract with the team, was already out with plantar fasciitis in his left foot since May 29. The scooter crash ensured he will miss the rest of the 2026 season. The Giants cited potential contract violations as the reason for suspending Bader's salary. The incident occurred while Bader was dealing with the initial injury, and the team is gathering details about the crash. Bader's suspension of pay is a direct result of the scooter accident, which has ended his season prematurely. The Giants' decision reflects the potential consequences of Bader's actions, which may have violated terms of his contract.

stories.headline: Chiefs rookie standout Cyrus Allen, Xavier Worthy injured at camp
stories.summary: Kansas City Chiefs wide receivers Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen left training camp with injuries on Saturday. Cyrus Allen, a fifth-round pick, suffered an apparent leg injury during a special teams coverage drill, and his status is currently unclear. The injuries deplete a position group that was disappointing last season and is in need of significant improvement this season. Allen had been a standout at camp, with Worthy previously praising his skills as an "electric route runner" with explosion and good ball skills. Worthy's own injury adds to the concern, as the Chiefs rely on improved wide receiver performance this season. The team is awaiting further evaluation on both players, and the extent of their injuries has not been disclosed. The losses could impact the Chiefs' depth at the wide receiver position.

stories.headline: Real Madrid close in on record €120m Yan Diomande deal as RB Leipzig star misses pre-season camp
stories.summary: Real Madrid is nearing a record €120m deal for RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande. The Ivory Coast international missed RB Leipzig's pre-season camp in Austria as negotiations with Real Madrid continue. The transfer package is valued at up to €132 million. Diomande's move to Real Madrid had previously stalled due to RB Leipzig's increased asking price. However, the Spanish giants appear to have agreed to the terms, and the deal is now in its advanced stages. The signing would be one of the summer transfer window's biggest acquisitions. Diomande's absence from RB Leipzig's pre-season camp suggests that a transfer is imminent, with Real Madrid set to complete the blockbuster signing. The deal would be a significant addition to Jose Mourinho's squad as part of the team's summer overhaul.

stories.headline: INEOS react to ‘agreement’ claim about Altay Bayindir and Celta de Vigo
stories.summary: Manchester United has reacted to claims of an agreement with Celta de Vigo for a loan deal involving Turkish goalkeeper Altay Bayindir. Spanish journalist Alberto Bravo reported that the two clubs had reached an agreement, with Bayindir set to complete a season-long loan next week. The potential move comes as Manchester United plans to bring in Orlando Gill as a replacement. The 35-year-old's arrival is believed to have paved the way for Bayindir's departure. INEOS, reportedly involved in the negotiations, has responded to the claims. While the details of the agreement are not fully disclosed, it is understood that Bayindir's loan move to Celta de Vigo is nearing completion, subject to final negotiations and formalities. The transfer is expected to be finalized in the coming days, marking a significant development in the summer transfer window.
